meta.name: Lime Chantilly
meta.yields: ~240g cream (10-12 piped rosettes — tops one 23cm tart)
meta.total_time: ~50 min (10 min active, 40 min passive — maceration + chill)
meta.description: Cream-cheese-stabilized lime whipped cream built for transport. Persian lime zest macerated into powdered sugar (Pierre Hermé / Dorie Greenspan smush trick), bloomed in softened cream cheese, then whipped with cold heavy cream. Holds piped peaks 24-48h refrigerated against an acidic curd surface. Designed as the topping for Tartine Lemon Cream Tart (lemon-on-lime pairing — Dominique Ansel's Salted Lemon Lime Tart precedent), but pairs with any citrus tart, berry pavlova, or summer fruit dessert.

change_log.summary: Initial recipe synthesized from 7-agent parallel research on cream-cheese-stabilized lime whipped cream. Heavy-ratio (50% CC) for transport hold; zest macerated into powdered sugar; juice optional fold at soft peaks.

vessels.name: Small Bowl
vessels.reuse: Maceration only — wash before chilling other items

vessels.name: Stand Mixer Bowl
vessels.reuse: Chill in freezer → CC smoothing → cream whipping (single bowl, no transfer)

vessels.name: Piping Bag
vessels.reuse: Fit with Ateco 869 French star or Wilton 1M tip; single-use

ingredients.name: Persian Lime Zest (microplaned)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 6/7 agents — modal value across lemon+lime WC recipes
ingredients.rationale: Persian lime safer than key lime for whipped applications (less bitter peel); ~2 tsp delivers clear lime identity without pith bitterness

ingredients.name: Powdered Sugar (10X with cornstarch)
ingredients.rationale: Cornstarch in 10X powdered sugar adds micro-stabilization; sweetens without overpowering

ingredients.name: Block Cream Cheese (full-fat, softened)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 7/7 agents — heavy-ratio cluster (50% CC:cream) for transport hold
ingredients.rationale: Block only (tub adds whey/gums that break the whip); H-E-B Organics Brick has cleanest label (locust bean gum only — the gum specifically associated with whipped cream stability). RecipeTin Eats Nagi tested this ratio holding 4 days piped on cake.

ingredients.name: Heavy Cream (cold, ≥36% fat)
ingredients.rationale: Cold straight from fridge — ATK measured fat-crystal-dependent whipping efficiency; warm cream won't form stiff peaks. H-E-B Heavy Whipping Cream (gellan-only stabilizer) is cleanest label at store; avoid Land O Lakes (carrageenan + polysorbate 80)

ingredients.name: Fresh Lime Juice (optional)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 2: 4-5 agents — fold late at soft peaks
ingredients.rationale: Lemon curd below already supplies acid; juice >1 tsp risks weep + curdle. Skip entirely for cleanest aroma; include 1 tsp for perceptible tang lift.

ingredients.name: Flake Salt (Maldon / fleur de sel)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Tier 2: chef precedent — Dominique Ansel Salted Lemon Lime Tart
ingredients.rationale: Maldon flake works as fleur de sel sub. Visible crystal + crunch + burst on tongue. Avoid table/iodized salt (dissolves on contact).

states.title: Zest Lime into Sugar
states.direction: Hold microplane at 45° over the small bowl. Light pressure, short strokes, rotate the lime constantly — stop the moment you see any white pith. Zest 1 Persian lime directly onto the 50g powdered sugar.
states.exit_condition: All green zest from one lime sits on top of the sugar; no visible white pith in the zest.

notes.text: Persian limes (the standard grocery store lime) work better here than key limes — less bitter peel, more forgiving if the microplane catches a touch of pith.

states.title: Smush & Rest (Maceration)
states.direction: Rub the zest into the sugar with your fingertips for 2-3 minutes until the sugar is damp, fragrant, and faintly green-tinged. Rest uncovered 15-30 minutes for oils to migrate into the sugar crystals.
states.exit_condition: Sugar appears damp and pale green; aroma is intensely lime-forward when sniffed.

notes.text: Known as the 'smush trick' (Pierre Hermé / Dorie Greenspan). Lime peel oils are fat- and sugar-soluble, not water-soluble — rubbing breaks the oil glands and binds the aromatics to the sugar crystals. Skipping this step yields noticeably less lime character in the finished cream.

states.title: Chill Mixer Bowl
states.direction: Place stand mixer bowl and whisk attachment in the freezer. Chill 15 minutes (overlap with the maceration rest).
states.exit_condition: Bowl and whisk are cold to the touch.

states.title: Rest Cream Cheese to Room Temp
states.direction: Cube 120g block cream cheese on the counter. Let sit 20-30 minutes (overlap with maceration). Target: pliable but cool, not warm. If still cold from fridge, add 5-10 min.
states.exit_condition: Cream cheese cubes yield to gentle finger pressure but are not visibly soft or shiny.

notes.text: Block only — never tub, whipped, or reduced-fat. Tub varieties add whey protein and pre-incorporated air that break the whip. H-E-B Organics Brick or Philadelphia Original are both reliable picks.

states.title: Smooth Cream Cheese Base
states.direction: Add softened cream cheese, lime-sugar (from maceration), salt, and vanilla to chilled mixer bowl. Beat on medium with whisk attachment 2-3 minutes until completely silky-smooth, scraping sides 2x. No lumps — point of no return.
states.exit_condition: Mixture is completely smooth, glossy, no visible lumps when scraped against the bowl. Spreads cleanly with rubber spatula.

notes.text: Lumps now = grain forever. If any cream cheese lump survives this step, cold cream will seize against it and the finished whip will be permanently grainy. Beat longer if needed.

states.title: Stream in Cold Cream
states.direction: With mixer on low, drizzle in about ¼ cup (60g) of the cold heavy cream over ~30 seconds to thin the cream cheese base. Then stream remaining cream slowly while running medium-high.
states.exit_condition: All cream incorporated, mixture thickened to a thin pourable consistency.

notes.text: Pouring too fast or dumping all at once causes the cold cream to shock the cream cheese into clumps. The slow stream is what keeps the emulsion smooth.

states.title: Whip to Stiff-ish Peaks
states.direction: Whip on medium-high 1-2 minutes until thickened to medium peaks. Drop to medium-low for last 20 seconds. Switch to hand whisk and finish to stiff-ish peaks (base upright, tip just folding). If using, fold in 1 tsp lime juice by hand at this stage.
states.exit_condition: Peaks hold their shape when whisk is lifted; tip folds slightly but base stays upright. Surface is smooth and glossy, not grainy.

notes.text: Window from stiff peaks to butter is narrow with cream cheese — finish by hand whisk for control. If it goes grainy (overwhipped), rescue by folding in 1-2 Tbsp fresh heavy cream by hand.

Lime juice is optional because acid can curdle whipped cream — the same mechanism that makes lemon juice curdle milk. Three things make 1 tsp safe here: the cream cheese stabilizer is already acid-tolerant, the juice is folded in late (after fat structure has formed), and the amount is small. The lemon curd below also supplies plenty of acidity. Adding 1 tsp gives a perceptible tang lift; skipping keeps the lime aroma cleaner. Either is correct.

states.title: Pipe Rosettes
states.direction: Transfer cream to piping bag fitted with Ateco 869 French star (or Wilton 1M). Pipe 10-12 evenly-spaced rosettes around the perimeter of the chilled tart, leaving the lemon-curd center exposed.
states.exit_condition: Perimeter ring of rosettes complete; rosettes sharp and upright; center curd still visible.

notes.text: French star (Ateco 869) has fine deep ridges that stay crisp through chilling. Wilton 1M is a good substitute — taller, chunkier swirls that forgive minor settling during transport.

states.title: Chill to Set Peaks
states.direction: Refrigerate dressed tart uncovered 1-2 hours so piped peaks set firm. After setting, can be loose-tented with foil propped up by toothpicks for transport. Finish with a flake of salt at destination just before serving.
states.exit_condition: Rosette surfaces feel firm to gentle finger pressure; peaks no longer move when bowl is jostled.

notes.text: Transport: insert toothpicks in the exposed curd center to keep foil off rosettes; loose-tent foil. Pack in cooler bag with 2 frozen gel packs (not loose ice) — target ≤8°C. Flat surface in car (floorboard/trunk, not seat). At destination: straight to fridge, hold until 20-30 min before serving, then microplane fresh lime zest over rosettes, sprinkle flake salt, optional channel-knife lime curl and viola/marigold/lemon thyme garnish.

methods.detail: If peaks soften after extended storage (>24h), transfer cream to a chilled bowl and whisk by hand 5-10 seconds to re-aerate. Will not fully recover original sharp peaks but presentable. Not applicable if already piped onto a tart — re-piping is the only fix at that point.

techniques.name: Maceration (smush trick)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Pierre Hermé via Dorie Greenspan; Janice Lawandi PhD; Half-Batch Baking
techniques.rationale: Rub zest into sugar 2-3 min, rest 15-30 min. Friction breaks oil glands and binds fat-soluble limonene/citral to sugar crystals. Highest-leverage flavor amplifier in citrus desserts.

techniques.name: Cream cheese as stabilizer at 50% ratio
techniques.sourcedFrom: Tier 1: 7/7 agents — heavy ratio cluster (Chelsweets, Always Eat Dessert, Nagi, Simply Stacie)
techniques.rationale: 120g CC per 240g cream holds piped peaks 24-48h refrigerated. Casein matrix + acid tolerance (CC already at pH ~4.5) lets it sit on acidic curd without breaking. Required for transport scenarios.

techniques.name: Soften CC + chill bowl + chill cream — temperature mismatch
techniques.rationale: Cream cheese soft (disperses smoothly), cream cold (whips properly). Mismatch is intentional. Cold-on-cold causes lumps that become permanent grain.

techniques.name: Stream cream slowly, finish by hand whisk
techniques.sourcedFrom: 5/7 agents — Style Sweet, Baking Mischief, Chelsweets
techniques.rationale: Dumping cold cream onto CC base seizes the cheese. Slow stream + medium speed emulsifies cleanly. Hand finish gives feel for the narrow stiff-peak-to-butter window.

techniques.name: Lime zest > lime juice; juice only at fold-in if at all
techniques.sourcedFrom: 6/7 agents — universal across lime WC recipes
techniques.rationale: Zest oils are fat-soluble (limonene + citral); juice is water + acid that destabilizes. >1 tsp juice per 240g cream risks weep. Lemon curd below already supplies acidity.

techniques.name: Persian lime over key lime for whipped applications
techniques.sourcedFrom: Lady Behind the Curtain, Sand Dollars and Lime
techniques.rationale: Persian (Tahiti) lime peel has less bitter compound concentration than key lime. Wider safety margin for microplane technique.
